subject: SLA: downtime liability, severity bands and remedies
messages:
From: Elin Svensson <elin@nordicpay.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: johan.eriksson@nordicpay.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 13:12:00 +0200
Subject: SLA remedies — proposal and required exit triggers

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looks promising. As we begin legal review, Procurement and Legal at NordicPay are pushing for stronger commercial remedies than standard service credits. Their asks are: a severity-tiered liability schedule (credits + capped monetary remedies), a right to terminate for repeated critical outages after a defined cure window, and an escrow-style fee-at-risk mechanism tied to uptime shortfalls for two consecutive quarters.

I attached a redline of the SLA annex with our suggested language (SLA_Proposed_Redlines.docx). High level:
- Severity 1 (P0) outages: monetary remedy equal to 5% of monthly committed fees per incident, cumulative cap of 25% monthly fee;
- Repeated S1 in a 90-day window = termination right after 30-day remediation attempt;
- Fee-at-risk: 10% of committed monthly fee withheld to an escrow account and released if SLA targets are met for the quarter.

I know this is outside standard vendor terms, but NordicPay is in a regulated payments vertical and must get board sign-off. Can we discuss what exceptions Redwood could accept (caps, timing, proof requirements)?

Regards,
Elin Svensson
Head of Procurement, NordicPay

Attachment: SLA_Proposed_Redlines.docx

Hi Elin — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Appreciated.

Quick response while we pull legal and product: Redwood understands that regulated fintechs need stronger contractual controls. We rarely agree to escrowed fee-withholding or uncapped termination rights, but we are open to a narrow, mutually measurable compromise.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal review (legal + SRE) — I’ve looped in Rishi (legal) and Marcus (product) to evaluate technical feasibility and commercial impact.
- Joint workshop — 60 minutes next week to go line-by-line on severity definitions and verify the incident measurement / adjudication process.
- Interim positions: please expect a counterproposal limiting monetary remedies, tightening thresholds for termination, and replacing an escrow with an indemnity/holdback construct tied to objective metrics.

Would Wed 2026-09-16 09:00 CEST work for a workshop?

Subject: RE: SLA remedies — proposal and required exit triggers

Team — quick legal/ops read. My initial analysis:

1) Monetary remedies vs. credits
- Redwoods standard is service credits that scale by downtime severity. Credits preserve predictability and cap ultimate vendor exposure. Uncapped cash damages or per-incident % fees materially increase our enterprise risk and will require approval from Finance and CEO.

2) Escrow / fee-withholding
- Holding 10% of committed fees in escrow is operationally complex (invoicing, revenue recognition, banking regs). As an alternative we can propose a short-term holdback (e.g., retainability on invoice for a single quarter) with precise release triggers and evidence requirements.

3) Termination triggers
- Termination for repeated critical outages is reasonable if narrowly defined: e.g., ">=3 Severity-1 incidents in any sliding 120-day window, each meeting the incident criteria and after at least two failed remediation attempts, with 30-day cure windows for each event." We should also require an independent incident audit (third-party) prior to termination.

4) Caps and aggregate liability
- We should propose a measurable cap: aggregate remedies (credits + cash) should be limited to the greater of 6 months of committed fees or 200% of the fees in the impacted month — whichever is lower. This protects both parties.

5) Measurement and adjudication
- Incident definitions must include concrete telemetry sources (region, model, sequence lengths) and a mutually agreed incident review board (1 rep from each party + neutral SRE).

I’ll draft counter-language that: replaces escrow with a 90-day invoice holdback, limits per-incident cash remedy to a defined % and sets a firm aggregate cap, and specifies termination only after an agreed adjudication and independent audit. I’ll attach a proposed draft by EOD.

– Rishi
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SLA_Annex_NordicPay_v2.pdf

From: Elin Svensson <elin@nordicpay.com>

Kimberly / Rishi — thanks for the fast turnaround and thoughtful positions. Johan and I reviewed Rishi's bullets and the notion of an independent post-incident audit is important to us. A few clarifying points:

- NordicPay can accept a replacement to escrow in the form of a 90-day holdback, provided we have a visible measurement dashboard and monthly reconciliations.
- We will not accept a cap below 3 months of committed fees for aggregate remedies; the board requires guaranteed minimum remediation liquidity.
- The termination threshold you suggested (3 S1s in 120 days) is in principle acceptable if the adjudication process includes an external auditor and the cure window only starts after the audit conclusion is shared.

Proposal: agree to the workshop on Wed 09:00 CEST to finalize wording. If you can circulate Rishi's draft SLA annex before the call, we’ll mark up the specific lines and bring our Head of Legal.

Regards,
Elin
Head of Procurement, NordicPay
